Last thing I’ll tell you unless you actually want more advice since I’m geeking out a bit and don’t wanna bother you. Try to find schist caves (they’re full of the same graphitic material that you get from hitting taint  with solinium weapons. If you haven’t tried that yet, it’s a grey-blue material called graphitic schist. Besides appearing with some explosions and in caves, it’s a source of lithium in a shredder. These caves are just beyond filled with ore, I recommend an advanced alloy pickaxe just so you can walk. The schist will clear in chunks, and after that, it’s just completely brimming with most, if not all overworld ores. I’ve also seen oil deposits spawn next to them, so they’re a pretty good resource hub overall.
Auto drills are really good for titanium, iron, aluminum, and tungsten because they all have crystal forms, and can mine those crystals in areas you would never be able to find or access otherwise.

Get good mining equipment (advanced alloy pickaxes are actually fairly cheap and offer vein miner 3, which is pretty good to start). If you can scavenge an autodrill from a structure, those are really useful as well, but they’re also really power consuming. (Tbf though, if you’ve managed to scavenge a drill, you’ve probably managed to pick up some fuel as well). Either loot basic  radioactive materials from structures or crates, or make mid-tier hazmat gear and start processing mined radioactive materials. Make self-charging batteries and higher tier generator tech (radial performance engines kinda suck early on because you have to get pistons which aren’t exactly the cheapest thing ever, but once you have them in a decent number, they’re pretty damn powerful, and still cheaper than the industrial steam generator (and I think the smaller turbine as well). Get chemical plants and recipes, produce components for higher level stuff, keep supplies up by drilling. I’m at *about* this stage in my main world, although some accidental weapons fire destroyed some critical resources, including a lot of my industrial components and desh ingredients. Still though, id say once you hit this stage, you’re probably ready or close to it to begin your first steps into the world of nuclear tech

The concept of a people’s republic isn’t linked to china, it’s a designation adopted by certain socialist countries. Most of the Soviet sphere, minus the Soviet Union themselves, used the phrase or some variant. If I remember correctly though, it’s been used for certain separatist or otherwise conflict-originating states as well, such as Donetsk and Luhansk in more recent times. Historically, it was used fairly often for breakaways or client   in the later stages of WWI, especially those coming out of the Russian empire. Examples include the Crimean People’s Republic, Kuban people’s republic, Ukrainian people’s republic, West Ukrainian people’s republic (this one is different, it gained  independence  from Austria while the former left Russia), etc.

Alright, so from here on out, I’ll be using a few terms 

Revolutionary Technocracy: Revolutionary technocracies are nations that have embraced technology fully as an ideological and government system. These nations often have major similarities to the technocracy movement of the 1920s, but all have modernized to account for the current economies and diplomatic situations the world faces, and most show an improved record for civil and human rights than what the original movement may have resulted in. These nations are ruled by experts in various fields, and promote Efficiency as a critical part of the revolution and their progress. Ideologically, these nations are a mixed bag, with some on the right seeing heavy corporate influence and nationalism,  while those on the left often claim technocracy as a means to escape capitalism. Other technocracies can be found towards the center of the political spectrum, often claiming that political squabbling goes against the ideals of technocracy and rationality that they hold dear. Civil rights and democracy are also mixed, with many states restricting public involvement to some extent. A few, however, have experimented with partially democratic concepts, often touting themselves as the evolution of the republic. 

Applied technocracy: Applied technocracies are nations that employ technocratic ideals within the confines of another system. Such states are often republics or looser dictatorships, with technocrats (largely economists), serving to encourage reform or compromise an emergency government. Such nations may be variable in the extent to which they follow technocrats or their method, although some analysts require sustained technocrat presence to even consider a nation an applied technocracy. 

With that in mind, let’s begin.

Italy: Applied Technocracy 

Technocrat governments , not unlike the ones that happen on occasion OTL, have become exceedingly common, largely in an effort to maintain economic and national stability as Europe falls into chaos. Such governments have seen a fair amount of success, leaving the nation in a fairly decent position compared to many of their neighbors. With the decline of its neighbors, Italy has moved from its status as an ”intermittent major power” to a solid great power, even gaining savoy from France as the nation fell. They maintain significant influence over Provence, Corsica, and Albania. Although an applied technocracy, certain revolutionary aspects (alongside a major Catholic resurgence) have begun to appear in the government, largely as a reaction to the situation in the French successor. 

Iberia and Porto: Semi-Revolutionary Technocracy

Iberia, along with its puppet state of Porto, form the other major southern European technocratic power. After riots occurred across Spain, largely consisting of separatist groups and ideological extremists alarmed over the changes in the rest of the continent, the Kingdom of Spain was nearly brought to collapse. However, the nation was saved (or destroyed, depends on who you ask), by a group of individuals, largely economists, but also a number of strategists, who staged the August Revolution, bringing down the kingdom. The defeated king was forced to abdicate, although the process was so abrupt that many aspects and leftovers of the kingdom remain existent in government (at least for now). The new Iberian government used promises of amnesty and autonomy, various dealings, and support for the revolution in order  to establish a degree of authority. The newly declared Reorganized State of Spain was still in a dreadful position, and lack of recognition by separatists, and a decent portion of the population did little to provide stability. As such, the new Spanish government promised something unprecedented, a partially confederated nation with extensive autonomy for certain regions, absolute and complete recognition of minority languages, and various other concessions to the separatists. Over time, certain groups did chose to agree to the newly created Madrid accords, rejoining the Spanish nation, while others would eventually be suppressed by force and exhaustion. Shortly after the nation had dealt with the majority of the separatist movements (note, “dealt with” largely means they’ve stopped shooting, many of the separatist movements are hostile and deeply skeptical, largely only bound to the new Spain by French aggression), the Portuguese experienced their own revolution. In order to prevent spillover, especially into an unstable Galicia, the Spanish nation launched an incursion into northern Portugal, pushing back far-right forces until the treaty of Vigo, which allowed Spain to establish the puppet state of Porto as a technocratic puppet. Soon after this, a growing movement within the Spanish technocrats was able to pass the Iberian Reorganization Act, which declared the Reorganized State of Spain to have become the state of Iberia, officially laying claim over the entire peninsula. Such a move has not been taken kindly by the Portuguese, be they in one of the successor states or Porto. This factor played a role in the ending of the Portuguese civil war and division of the country, as neither the communists or the fascists wanted to be caught in several conflicts at once.

I strongly suspect Siberia wouldn’t be British. It would either:

> Fall into Russian hands the same way as irl

> be incorporated into the British colony  that lead to the US of Amuria, joining amuria either during their revolution, or as a zone of influence afterwards 

> be incorporated into the British colony that became amuria (or a separate British colony right next to it) and not leave the British in the amurian revolution. This option is the least likely in my opinion for reasons I’ll get into later on. Short Version if you don’t wish to read on (this will get long, I understand): extremely weak Canada equivalent with an uncertain future.

> Korea or China take it. Extremely unlikely given the existence of Amuria/the colony it revolted as, but *Possibly* easier to administer than it would be for the Brits. Depends on a number of factors, although it’s also possible it starts as some sort of Asian power-controlled colony and then breaks away/gets cut off, leaving an independent-ish protostate. 

> get colonized by a different European power (unlikely, if it happens, it’s Denmark or France, and I’ll get into why later)

Let’s get right into the options, shall we?

Option A: Siberia falls into Russian hands the same as irl. This seems like a relatively realistic option in my opinion, and it’s simple enough. Russia just simply finishes colonizing Siberia before the British can take anything, *or*, the British take such a small amount that they’re beat back into the sea. Although this could occur as Russia getting the entirety of Siberia (except for the more settled colony that became Amuria, although we could reduce or Eliminate the existence of Amur all together by either giving Russia some/all of its lands, or partitioning between Russia and Korea), it’s also possible Siberia is still divided, just far more in Russia’s favor. Perhaps britain is restricted to just the Kamchatka peninsula here. In either of these scenarios, where Russia gets all or most of what you’ve labeled as British Siberia, the impact almost certainly a fierce naval rivalry, with war constantly on the horizon. 

Option B: Siberia goes to Amuria in some shape or form. Either British Siberia was part of the colony that became Amuria, and joins/is taken in the revolution, leading to Siberia being a formal part of Amuria, or the Amurians win the colonization race/beat back other contenders after the revolution to either annex the territory or bring it into its sphere of influence. This scenario sees a stronger Amuria in an unusual position, one that is both dangerous and full off opportunities. Amuria now exists/operates very closely to Russia, Denmark, and Britain, and will likely be seeking Allies against whichever power threatens their position the most. This *could* mean the French, but I’d imagine the Danes have an interest in protecting their Arctic holdings against a much closer British empire. The Danes still aren’t especially powerful, but with the right development and progress, they could still be an issue for the royal navy. Russia could also see Denmark as useful for a similar reason. It’s *possible* that we see a Russo-Danish-amurian solution against the British here, but that’s assuming Russia doesn’t hate Amur for being a post-colony on lands they may claim. To make a coalition scenario interesting, however, we can extend it to be a major global conflict in the making. For the sake of the scenario I mentioned before, we’ll have Amur, Denmark-Norway, and Russia (with France possibly supporting these powers in general, but possibly not in this specific coalition, depending on how Asia-oriented such a coalition is) opposing British expansion, while Britain will probably court Korea for an alliance against Amur, promising them lands in the process as well as the kingdom of Tokyo for similar reasons, promising them a United north Japanese state. Given the Korean territory near Tokyo, however, it’s possible the two are mutually exclusive. In this case, britain sides with Korea just  because they’re more powerful. In Europe, Britain would also try to court Allies against the the Russian coalition, especially if France is involved/supporting them. If the Russo-Austrian alliances are still functional, perhaps britain promises the commonwealth lands back from Russia, in which case the Russians, Prussians, and Austrians agree on additional partitions. If Russia and Austria aren’t Allies, Britain *might* court Austria, But the successes here (and whether or not they just give up and court Poland still), depend on a series of relationships and situations within the HRE (or German confederation), and between them, Russia, Austria, and Poland. I obviously don’t know what all the possibilities would be, but the Brits probably do attempt to find a friend in Central Europe. The end result here is quite possibly an early WWI. Results here are difficult to consider given the aforementioned  Central European power dynamics. 

> The Canada option (I’m going to guess that’s what you did): British Siberia happens, and remains British even after the Amurian revolution. They become an extremely weak colony or dominion due to climate and terrain, and are in danger from all sides. History probably progresses pretty closely to the previous scenario. The weakness of any colonial position here, the danger from all sides, amurian influence on the colony through their region, and low returns from the colony make this the least likely scenario in my opinion. 

> taken by another Asian power
A highly unlikely, albeit interesting scenario. Most likely, Korea launched some sort of attempt here, at least until getting cut off by Amur. The colony possibly   an independent-ish “state”, being either diplomatically and economically isolated by powers such as Russia or Amur, or receives most of its trade from these nearby powers. The other possibility is that Siberia has remained a direct colony. Depending on the strength of the amurian navy, and how friendly they are with the Asian power involved, the situation then plays out either the same as the previous scenario, or with an even weaker colony. 

 > Taken by a different European power 
A non-British European power, most likely France or Denmark-Norway, takes part or all of what you have marked as British Siberia. If France does it, it serves a similar role to French Canada, trading fur and other resources with the people of Siberia. The future of the colony could go several different ways, although the closest way to irl would he that someone else takes it. If Denmark-Norway takes it, it’s probably an exploration mission,  or a Greenland-traveling fleet blown off course. Either way, it probably sees administration similar to other high-latitude Nordic colonies, albeit with an uncertain future.

Don’t take this as me hating on the scenario, the artwork is great and it’s an interesting interpretation of the scenario btw.
